body.estimand_functional: \(D_k(n)=\max_{(G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k},\ d_e(G)<\infty}[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]\), with finite fibers represented by \(p_e(t)\)

sampling_model.design: The identification layer uses the exact population covariance of a known recursive Gaussian mixed graph. The estimation layer uses independent observational sampling at fixed \(G,n\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal query is the direct structural coefficient \(\lambda_e\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: When \(d_e(G)<\infty\), project \(S_m\) smoothly onto the regular covariance-model stratum, evaluate the certificate circuits and \(p_e\), isolate every simple real root, and retain roots by exact local real-extension status. When \(d_e(G)=\infty\), the symbolic stage reports transcendence and the finite-set inference rung does not apply.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: TreeID introduced the missing-bidirected-cycle method for tree-shaped linear SEMs; the 2022 paper did not itself prove completeness, while Gupta--Bläser later established the complete per-edge \(1/2/\infty\) classification and Briefs--Bläser explicitly reports TreeID as complete in light of that result.
Theorem 27 gives the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) trichotomy for rooted directed trees and therefore the finite-degree upper boundary two.
Theorem 1 gives an \(O(n^3\log^2 n)\) randomized implementation of the same complete tree-only \(1/2/\infty\) predicate.
The paper gives polynomial-time sufficient and necessary-side graphical criteria, full-fiber mixed-component decomposition, and small-graph finite-degree computations.
Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4 transfer rational identification of coefficients from ancestral induced subgraphs to the full graph.
Corollary 6 places generic edge identifiability in polynomial space without returning an algebraic coordinate eliminant.
Theorems 4.4 and 5.1 search for minimum bounded-degree rational identifying formulas and give quasi-polynomial computation for a fixed formula-degree bound.
Theorem 2.1 constructs a generic rational univariate representation for generically zero-dimensional parametric polynomial systems and later results control specialization outside explicit bad loci.
The paper computes separating forms, rational univariate representations, isolating boxes, and exact signs for bivariate polynomial systems.
The paper derives consistency, rates, and confidence regions for criterion-defined identified sets by sample-criterion inversion.
The preprint derives influence functions, asymptotic normality, and Wald inference for rational half-trek estimators.
The paper distinguishes global real identifiability from generic algebraic behavior and analyzes explicit degree-two failures of injectivity.

body.tldr: Adding a bounded number of parents to a supplied rooted directed tree creates a finite algebraic ambiguity regime not summarized by whole-fiber cardinality. The focal object is the sharp single-coordinate complex degree frontier \(D_k(n)\). The project derives the exact frontier for every size and excess-edge budget through a projection-aware orientation-realization recurrence, proves the universal \(2^{k+1}\) ceiling and an attaining one-sink family for \(n\ge2k+4\), and turns the proof into a fixed-parameter minimal-polynomial and exceptional-set certificate. A separate real lifting test filters complex roots, and regular finite-set inference estimates every retained branch at the root-\(m\) rate without branch selection.

project_justification.gap: Existing tree algorithms and general mixed-graph work study identification decisions, rational recovery, whole-parameter fibers, or unparameterized elimination. No result determines the maximum finite extension degree of one directed coefficient as a function of both graph size and the number of extra parents.
project_justification.niche: Distance from a supplied arborescence creates a parameterized algebraic regime in which ordinary vertices retain Möbius structure while at most \(2k\) exceptional incoming coefficients form a coupled quadratic core. The hard boundary is whether constrained covariance coefficients realize the multihomogeneous orientation count at every smaller size.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves a projection-aware upper bound, constructs branch-separating graph families, resolves the all-size orientation-realization recurrence, and supplies minimal-polynomial, exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference guarantees in the output format required by an extension of fasttreeid.

body.related_work: Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz introduced TreeID for tree-shaped linear SEMs: the 2022 paper developed the missing-bidirected-cycle method and a polynomial-space procedure, but did not itself prove completeness. Gupta and Bläser later established the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) classification through rank-one anchoring, Möbius propagation, cycle closure, and polynomial identity testing; that result is used solely as the cited \(k=0\) boundary, while the sharp-size question begins at positive excess-arrow budget. Briefs and Bläser explicitly report TreeID as complete in light of the later Gupta--Bläser result, accelerate the tree predicate, and implement it in fasttreeid; the proposed algorithm enlarges its graph and symbolic-output domain, without claiming a better \(k=0\) running time. The novelty claim is reserved for finite single-coordinate degrees beyond this tree trichotomy. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton develop half-trek criteria, factor whole generic fibers across mixed components, and exhibit higher-degree small SEMs, which makes a lone cubic or quartic non-novel and motivates the single-coordinate projection distinction. Drton and Weihs show that ancestral subgraphs can identify individual coefficients, but their reduction stops at rational identification rather than extension degree. Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz give a complete polynomial-space generic edge decision procedure; the fixed-parameter theorem strengthens its output on the tree-plus-\(k\) class to the exact degree, minimal polynomial, and bad-locus certificate. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma optimize bounded-degree rational formulas, a different degree notion from algebraic branch degree. Corniquel, Jeronimo and Sabia, Emiris, and Bouzidi et al. provide generic RUR, circuit-resultant, sparse-elimination, and real-isolation machinery that informs the certificate construction but does not prove covariance-residual sparsity or coordinate preservation. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer provide the identified-set inference architecture, Drton diagnoses nonstandard behavior at singularities, and Mareis, Sturma, and Drton derive regular half-trek influence functions; the statistical rung is restricted to separated simple algebraic branches and makes no discriminant-uniform claim.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The orientation coefficient is only an upper envelope until covariance-coefficient relations, \(S_G\)-localization, affine dehomogenization, and projective infinity are controlled. The rooted five-node characteristic-zero census is the explicit kill test: a strict loss must alter the all-size recurrence rather than be hidden by the large-size family. The modular quartic and the degree-eight and degree-sixteen rational checks are evidence, not statements. Coordinate-preserving localization must never be promoted to equality of full fibers. Real roots are never equated with real supported lifts, and local Jacobian rank is never used to claim real uniqueness.
body.honest_scope: All formal nodes are to be proved. The all-\(n\) recurrence and attaining families are the open kernel; the large-size exponent is supporting traction and cannot replace it. The algorithmic theorem must cost every slice, \(S_G\)-localization, incidence lift, affine dehomogenization, coefficient descent, circuit gate, and identity-test error. On a transcendental query it returns exactly \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\) and no minimal polynomial or polynomial-dependent exceptional-set object. Statistical inference is confined to fixed finite-degree queries and nonempty compact subsets of smooth connected real-model cells outside the certified exceptional set, with locally constant real-extension status. Certificate-denominator, simple-root derivative, and branch-separation margins are conclusions of compactness, continuity, monic Cauchy bounds, and the squarefreeness factor in \(h_{G,e}\), not assumptions. The finite-sample estimator may be empty off its validity event, but its emptiness probability vanishes uniformly and Hausdorff loss uses the explicit empty-set convention. No inference uniform over discriminants, no automatic branch selection, and no all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed. Positive definiteness of a recovered disturbance matrix follows by congruence from a complete real supported lift and positive-definite \(\Sigma\). Separate explicit residual checks supply the exact small-size maxima. The singleton real-fiber reduction yields ordinary asymptotic normality.
